title: Experiment Tracking and Model Registry with MLflow
intro: Six months from now, someone will ask 'which data and hyperparameters produced the model in production?'. Experiment tracking is how you answer that in seconds instead of never.

steps.prompt: Launch the MLflow UI locally to browse runs.
steps.explanation: Every logged run — params, metrics, artifacts — is browsable at localhost:5000.
steps.why: For a team, point everyone at one shared tracking server (MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI) instead of local mlruns/ folders, or experiments stay trapped on individual laptops.

steps.prompt: List all runs in experiment 1 from the terminal.
steps.explanation: Each run has a unique ID that ties metrics, params, and the model artifact together.
steps.why: Run IDs are what make a model traceable: a production model that references run a1b2c3d4e5 can always be traced back to its exact code, data, and hyperparameters.

steps.prompt: Reproduce a training run from this project's MLproject file with a specific learning rate.
steps.fake_output:
=== Created directory /tmp/tmpx for downloading remote URIs ===
=== Running command 'python train.py --learning_rate 0.01' ===
=== Run (ID 'b2c3d4e5f6') succeeded ===
steps.explanation: The MLproject file defines the entry point, environment, and parameters, so anyone can rerun it identically.
steps.why: Being able to rerun training from a single command is what separates a reproducible project from a pile of notebooks.

steps.prompt: Serve the model from run a1b2c3d4e5 locally on port 5001 to sanity-check it.
steps.explanation: The exact logged artifact is now behind a REST endpoint.
steps.why: Testing the logged artifact — not the in-memory model from your notebook — catches serialization and dependency problems before deployment.

steps.prompt: Send a test prediction to the served model.
steps.explanation: A 7% fraud probability for this transaction.
steps.why: A quick smoke test with a known input and known expected output is the ML equivalent of a health check — worth automating in CI for every candidate model.
